01.event: would carry a lamp in R. Yehoshua ben Levi's place but not in R. Yohanan's
01.summary: Rabbi Abbahu used to move a lamp on Shabbat where R. Yehoshua ben Levi ruled, and refrained where R. Yohanan ruled, out of deference. The Gemara explains his practice and how he informed his servant.
01.missing: a one-time event and any consequence; this is a habitual practice cited as evidence
01.reason: A report of a sage's habitual practice cited as evidence, with the rest Gemara analysis; nothing follows from it.

02.event: visited the house of the son of a vinegar strainer and examined them
02.summary: Rav came to the house of Bar Shapi Halla and had them examined; the Gemara debates whether the examination concerned lineage or silence.
02.missing: what the examination found and any consequence
02.reason: A single act alluded to as evidence inside a legal discussion, with no change or outcome narrated.

03.missing: any narrated event; this is a calendrical derivation from verses about Moses
03.reason: Exegetical derivation of Moses' birth and death dates; no narrative, and biblical in any case.

04.event: an incident in which he gave an orphan one-twelfth of the estate
04.summary: Rav Adda bar Ahava reports an incident where Rabbi gave an orphan daughter one-twelfth of her father's estate as dowry; the Gemara uses it to reconcile rulings.
04.missing: the incident itself; only the ruling is given
04.reason: Only a ruling in an alluded case; no other narrated action or change.

05.actor: an Arab (seen by Rabba bar bar Hana)
05.event: cut open his camel with a sword
05.turn: the camel died before it could stop braying
05.outcome: Abaye explains the camel was emaciated
05.summary: Rabba bar bar Hana saw an Arab cut open his camel with a sword; the camel died so fast it did not finish braying. Abaye explains it away as an emaciated animal.
05.missing: any human response or development; it is a one-line eyewitness report cited as evidence
05.reason: A one-line eyewitness wonder with two linked events, cited in legal discussion; the open case between report and incident, so borderline.

06.actor: the widow of Rav Yosef son of Rav Menashya
06.event: came before Rav Yosef and asked for sustenance, wine, and silk
06.turn: he apportioned sustenance and wine, then questioned the silk
06.outcome: she retorts she needs it for him and his colleagues
06.summary: A widow comes before Rav Yosef demanding support; he apportions food and wine, balks at silk, and she answers that she needs it so as not to be shamed before him and his colleagues.
06.reason: A courtroom exchange where the rabbi's apportioning is an act that changes something, like Ketubot 65a:10, but mostly dialogue and without a stated outcome.

07.event: the Sages ask where R. Elai is
07.summary: The Sages ask Rabbi Abbahu where Rabbi Elai is hiding, and he answers in a cryptic wordplay implying Elai is sleeping after his wedding night.
07.missing: any action beyond speech; the implied marriage is only alluded to
07.reason: A question and a clever answer, with no conflict and no event; speech only.

08.actor: Rav Pappa and Rav Huna son of Rav Yehoshua
08.event: planned to rule that a nursing mother may remarry immediately
08.turn: an old woman told them Rav Nahman had forbidden it in her case; Rav Pappi cited a baraita against them
08.outcome: they admitted they had forgotten; the halakha is settled, and an incident of a woman strangling her child is mentioned and dismissed
08.summary: Two sages were about to rule leniently when an old woman told them of her own case where Rav Nahman forbade it; Rav Pappi then challenged them and they conceded they had forgotten. The Gemara concludes the halakha and dismisses a reported incident of a woman who strangled her child.
08.missing: what they finally did in the case; much is legal discussion
08.reason: Mainly speech, but there is an intervention and a change of course; the legal discussion between is not story. Borderline under R-C7 shape 1.

09.outcome: he ruled the oath rule applies only to a ketubah
09.summary: A case came before Rabbi Yitzhak in Antioch and he ruled that collecting in the husband's absence applies only to a woman's ketubah, not a creditor.
09.missing: the facts of the incident and any change
09.reason: A case before a rabbi and his ruling; coming before him is the only event.

10.actor: R. Elai and R. Yaakov bar Zavdi
10.event: were sitting when R. Shimon bar Abba passed and they stood for him
10.turn: he told them they need not stand
10.outcome: he gave two reasons; no further outcome
10.summary: Two sages sitting in study rose when Rabbi Shimon bar Abba passed by. He told them they need not, since they were ordained and he was not, and since Torah does not stand before its students.
10.missing: any response or consequence after his words
10.reason: Real events (passing, standing) then a teaching speech, with little change; borderline under R-C7.

11.actor: a man whose yevama lived in Bei Hoza'a
11.event: came before R. Hanina asking whether to go down to Babylonia
11.turn: R. Hanina answered harshly about his brother
11.summary: A man asked Rabbi Hanina whether he could go to Babylonia to perform levirate marriage; Rabbi Hanina replied that his brother had married a Samaritan and died, blessed be God, and should he follow?
11.reason: A question and answer framed by a visit; the setting is not a second event and nothing follows.

12.actor: a woman obliged to take an oath in Rav Beivai's court
12.event: the opposing litigant demanded the oath be in town
12.turn: she demanded a document of rights first, and Rav Beivai ordered it written
12.outcome: Rav Pappi mocked Rav Beivai's ruling
12.summary: A woman was obligated to swear; her opponent wanted the oath in public, hoping she would be ashamed. She demanded a written document first, Rav Beivai ordered it, and Rav Pappi derided him for it.
12.missing: whether she swore or anything changed
12.reason: After the woman comes to court it is all dialogue, with conflict and an order; borderline under R-C7 shape 1.

13.event: went to villages and was asked about an eiruv with moist beans
13.turn: he did not know the answer
13.outcome: returning to the study hall, he was told R. Yannai's ruling
13.summary: Rabbi Yirmeya visited villages where he was asked a halakhic question he could not answer. When he returned to the study hall he was told Rabbi Yannai's ruling.
13.missing: any change beyond learning the answer
13.reason: Mostly a question and answer, but with a journey, a failure and a return; between borderline and not, so borderline.

14.actor: the judges of Nehardea and Rav Hana bar Bizna
14.event: ruled and collected sustenance from movable property
14.turn: Rav Nahman ordered them to reverse
14.outcome: he threatened to seize their houses
14.summary: Courts in Nehardea and Pumbedita collected support for daughters from movable property. Rav Nahman ordered them to reverse their rulings or he would take their houses.
14.reason: Rulings and a collection followed by a threatening order; conflict and an act, but the outcome is not narrated.

15.summary: Judges ruled in accordance with Rabbi Tarfon, and Reish Lakish overturned their ruling. Rabbi Yohanan criticized him for treating it like a Torah-law error.
15.reason: A ruling reversed is an act that changes something, with conflict, but the episode is sketched in one line.

16.event: came before Rabbi Ami demanding her ketubah
16.turn: he dismissed her; she argued about her old age
16.outcome: he ruled the husband must be forced to divorce
16.summary: A childless woman demanded her ketubah from Rabbi Ami; he sent her away as not commanded to procreate. She asked who would care for her in old age, and he reversed, ruling to compel the husband.
16.reason: Dialogue with conflict and a change of the rabbi's mind; mainly speech, so borderline.

17.outcome: the Gemara explains there were rumors about him and his mother-in-law
17.summary: A son-in-law passed by the door of his father-in-law's house and Rav Sheshet had him flogged; the Gemara explains he was suspected with his mother-in-law.
17.missing: detail; cited as evidence in a list of Rav's practices
17.reason: Two linked events (passing, flogging) told in one line as evidence; weak development, so borderline.

18.event: went to learn from R. Elazar ben Shamua
18.turn: the students ganged up on him like roosters
18.summary: Rabbi went to study with Rabbi Elazar ben Shamua, but the students set upon him like aggressive roosters and would not let him learn. He came away with only one teaching from the Mishnah.
18.reason: A post-biblical sage acts, meets conflict, and the outcome changes what he learned: events, conflict and change.

19.actor: the daughter of Nakdimon ben Guryon
19.event: the Sages allotted her 400 gold coins for perfume
19.turn: she said: so may you allot for your daughters
19.summary: When the Sages awarded Nakdimon ben Guryon's daughter four hundred gold coins for perfume, she told them to allot the same for their own daughters, and they answered Amen.
19.missing: the later turn of her fate lies outside the passage
19.reason: A ruling followed by a pointed exchange; the apportioning is an act, but the rest is speech with little change.

20.actor: Rav Anan bar Tahalifa; Rav Ashi
20.event: standing before Shmuel / Rav Kahana when food was brought
20.outcome: otherwise he would have been endangered
20.summary: Rav Anan recalls standing before Shmuel when mushrooms were brought; had Shmuel not shared, he would have been endangered. Rav Ashi tells the same of Rav Kahana and turnip in vinegar.
20.missing: real development; these are first-person reports cited as evidence for a rule
20.reason: Small first-person incidents with an act (giving food) and implied consequence, cited as evidence; weak change, so borderline rather than not.
